fields.quote: Retry filtering makes every delivery exactly once
fields.rationale: Source body records the author claim that the change 'makes delivery exactly once'. Contract 2 says a send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits and supplies no deduplication or idempotency contract. functions.mjs after still retries when error.retryable is true. probe-results.json after.duplicate.effects is 2. after.concurrentCalls sums to 2 effects. Retry filtering does not make every delivery exactly once.
source.json title is 'Cedar Relay: filter retries and increase delays'. The eyebrow repeats that product name.

fields.quote: Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
fields.rationale: after in functions.mjs throws when !error.retryable. probe-results.json after.permanent.calls is 1, delays [], error 'permanent'. after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20], matching sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt). Contract 2 supplies no deduplication. Contract 3 says delays are requested milliseconds. The dek does not treat the exhausted example as a universal delivery guarantee.
probe-results.json assumptions: 'Deterministic modeled send outcomes and immediate sleep promises; no timing or production measurement.' The meta names that evidence class.

fields.quote: A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
fields.rationale: Contract 2: 'A send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits.' probe.mjs duplicate uses { effect: true, error: transient } then a second effect. probe-results.json after.duplicate.effects is 2. 'Can' matches the modeled possibility.
Section label only. It does not assert a fact about the contracts, functions, or probe.

fields.quote: The old loop retried every rejection
fields.rationale: before in functions.mjs has no retryable check. It sleeps and continues until attempt === retries. probe-results.json before.permanent.calls is 2 after a permanent error, then result 'delivered'.

fields.quote: The old loop retried rejected sends until the retry budget ran out. It requested a ten-millisecond delay between attempts.
fields.rationale: before retries on catch until attempt === retries, then throws. await sleep(10) is the only delay. probe-results.json before.exhausted.calls is 3 with retries 2; delays [10, 10]. Contract 3: delays are requested milliseconds.
Section label only. It does not assert a fact about the contracts, functions, or probe.
after catches, then throws if !error.retryable || attempt === retries, else await sleep(...). Classification happens before wait. after.permanent has delays [] and one call.

fields.quote: The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error. With a budget of two retries, retryable failures request delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds before the final send. This permits up to three sends. A rejected sleep prevents the next send.
fields.rationale: after.permanent.calls is 1 and error is 'permanent'. With retries 2, after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20] and calls is 3, matching sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt) on attempt 0 and 1 then a final send. The three-send bound is scoped to that budget, not a universal cap. after.sleepFailure.calls is 1 and error is 'sleep-failed', matching contract 3 that sleep rejection propagates.
Section label only. It does not assert a fact about the contracts, functions, or probe.

fields.quote: A retry can duplicate a remote effect
fields.rationale: Contract 2 allows rejection after the effect commits and supplies no deduplication. probe-results.json after.duplicate.effects is 2. 'Can' is modal and matches the modeled case.

fields.quote: The author describes exactly-once delivery, but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits. The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects. Separate invocations share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism.
fields.rationale: source.json body: 'The author says this avoids retrying permanent failures and makes delivery exactly once.' Contract 2 permits rejection after commit and has no deduplication or idempotency. probe.mjs duplicate comment and after.duplicate.effects 2 match the lost-acknowledgment example. Contract 4: separate calls share no retry counter and no lock or cross-call exclusion. after.concurrentCalls is two successful one-effect traces.
Section label only. It does not assert a fact about the contracts, functions, or probe.

before.permanent.calls is 2; after.permanent.calls is 1. after throws on !error.retryable. The modeled permanent case retries less than the old loop. This is the modeled comparison, not a delivery guarantee.

fields.quote: The change filters failures and increases requested delays. It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.
fields.rationale: after filters on error.retryable and uses 10 * 2 ** attempt versus before's sleep(10). The loop is attempt <= retries inside one call. Contract 4: separate calls share no retry counter. Contract 2 and after.duplicate.effects 2 show it does not bound successful delivery or duplicates. Passing exhausted/permanent examples do not prove universal delivery.

missing_material_limitations_note: Contracts 2–4 appear in /dek, /footer, /sections/1/content, /sections/2, and /sections/3/content (no dedup, requested delays, sleep rejection propagates, per-invocation attempt bound, no cross-call exclusion). The title omits those limits; that omission is graded as /title contradicted, not as a gap in the rest of the artifact. Idempotency is not named as a word; duplicate-effect and no-dedup wording cover the same contract. Wall-clock versus requested duration is carried by the word 'requested' plus /meta.

attribution_errors.quote: Retry filtering makes every delivery exactly once
attribution_errors.rationale: source.json body attributes exactly-once delivery to the author as a claim. The title states that claim as a fact about retry filtering. /sections/2/content later attributes the claim to the author and contradicts it. The title is the attribution error.

reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: Reader-facing copy names 'the supplied contract' as an evaluation artifact. A walkthrough would state the send rule without pointing at the review packet.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects.
reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: Trace language ('modeled' example 'records' effects) matches probe commentary rather than a reader explanation of lost acknowledgments.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism
reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: Near-verbatim contract 4 phrasing ('retry counter', 'delivery exclusion') leaks review-packet wording into the section.

quotes.quote: Retry filtering makes every delivery exactly once
Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
With a budget of two retries, retryable failures request delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds before the final send. This permits up to three sends.
A retry can duplicate a remote effect
It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.

reader_facing_prose.rationale: Most body fields match the functions and probe and avoid universal delivery claims. The title still asserts exactly-once delivery for every delivery. That universal claim is false in the supplied contract and in after.duplicate / after.concurrentCalls. A passing example (permanent stops in one call; delays 10 then 20) does not prove exactly-once delivery. Later corrections do not make the title accurate.

unresolved_uncertainty: Whether /meta 'Deterministic modeled examples' should be nonfactual framing instead of supported. Graded supported because it matches probe-results.json assumptions.
Whether section eyebrows ('The setting', 'The change', 'The boundary', 'The short version') should be unsupported rather than nonfactual. Graded nonfactual as labels with no source predicate.
Whether 'stop immediately' in /dek could be read as a timing claim. Graded as no-retry, matching after.permanent (1 call, no delay).
Whether reviewer-language leakage in /sections/2/content should flip that field's prose rating from pass to uncertain. Factual status remains supported; leakage is listed separately.
Whether omitting the word 'idempotency' while stating no dedup and duplicate effects is a missing material limitation. Left empty; the same contract is otherwise stated.
method_notes: Used only manifest.json, fields.json, source.json, functions.mjs, probe.mjs, and probe-results.json. Did not infer authorship or editing. Passing probe examples were not treated as universal guarantees. Observed contradictions (title versus contract 2 and duplicate/concurrent probe results) are listed separately from uncertainties.
